title: Book 5 — Terpsichore, Chapter 83
paragraphs: During this time, and also before this, the Aeginetans were subjects of the Epidaurians, and among other things they were accustomed to cross over to Epidaurus to have their private lawsuits settled. After this time, however, they built ships for themselves and revolted from the Epidaurians out of willfulness. Being at odds with them, they kept on doing them damage, since in fact they had command of the sea; and especially they stole from them these very images of Damia and Auxesia, bringing them and setting them up in the interior of their own country at a place called Oea, which is about twenty furlongs from their city. Having set them up in this place, they worshipped them with sacrifices and with choruses of women accompanied by scurrilous jesting, ten men being appointed for each of the deities to provide the choruses. The choruses spoke evil of no man, but only of the women of the place. The Epidaurians too had the same rites; and they also have rites which may not be divulged.
